question: Should Browser CLI preserve existing unrestricted `--fields-file` compatibility, or formally adopt a 1 MiB hard limit for existing automation?
rationale: The code and tests can enforce either behavior, but neither the prior implementation nor an established public contract selects the acceptable upgrade behavior for users with larger files.

options.title: Require an approved size contract
options.body: Keep the PR paused until a Browser CLI owner explicitly confirms the 1 MiB limit and the intended upgrade behavior for existing automation.

options.title: Preserve existing compatibility
options.body: Remove the new hard rejection and pursue a resource-control approach that does not reject previously accepted fields files unless a future contract is approved.

options.title: Accept the breaking limit
options.body: Merge the cap as an intentional compatibility break after maintainers accept that existing files above 1 MiB will fail.

recommendation.title: Require an approved size contract
recommendation.body: Keep the PR paused until a Browser CLI owner explicitly confirms the 1 MiB limit and the intended upgrade behavior for existing automation.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision concerns the Browser CLI's user-facing compatibility contract, not a narrow test or implementation correction.
